newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures cut gains late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures cut gains late, end mixed.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures cut gains in closing trade, finishing a choppy session mixed.
Traders said most units edged off late on pre-weekend long profittaking in otherwise light afternoon turnover following a fairly busy morning.

"There was nothing significant," said one floor broker of the close. "Everything pulled back a little. But they basically were watching bonds and S&Ps. During the morning, currencies were trading on their own."
He said price boards showed estimated volume in March yen and marks of 25,000 contracts each, with 20,000 Swiss francs.

Currencies had mirrored moves in U.S. stocks and, to a lesser degree, bonds. Both markets fell to moderate to large losses, with Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500s subsequently whipping around in erratic trade.
"Clearly, everything was being driven for the better part by S&Ps," added the floor broker.

Technical buying also lifted marks, yen and Swiss francs, which each retraced a portion of losses in markets that many analysts still see as fundamentally weak. But the dollar's inability to keep rising Friday after scoring overnight gains made some look for more upside currency retracement first.
"Below 1.4110 Swiss, 1.6330 marks and 119.30 yen, the dollar is weak," added the broker of the very nearterm outlook.
The currency advance also likely prompted more pre-weekend covering as traders chewed over the possibility of central bank intervention with the yen rising rather than falling.
"There are a lot of questions out there," said the broker. "The BoJ would probably want to intervene on a (yen) rally."
March yen overnight slid to a new contract low at $0.008386 as the dollar probed above the critical 120.00 yen level for the first time in nearly four years.
Comments overnight from some Japanese goverment officials also stoked intervention fears, brokers said.
Marks garnered support from German state inflation figures showed enough strength to suggest to traders that the Bundesbank might not cut rates again soon.

But a Bundesbank spokesman Friday quoted vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum as saying the central bank's decision to inject extra funds into the money market signalled German monetary policy will remain steady in the nearterm.
The Canadian dollar fell, with brokers attributing much of its decline to spreads against the buoyant Swiss franc.

But the broker wondered aloud about the reasoning behind sales of the Canadian dollar against the Swiss unit, saying that selling the U.S. dollar in order to buy the Swiss franc likely would also depress the Canadian dollar as well.

At the end of pit trading, March yen rose $0.000049 to $0.008465, marks rose $0.0035 to $0.6156, Swiss francs gained $0.0074 to $0.7140, sterling eased $0.0008 to $1.6262, Canadian dollar fell $0.0033 to $0.7438, Aussie dollar lost $0.0004 to $0.7713, Mexican peso fell $0.000275 to $0.124825.
